title: Layer Stacker
description: Stack layers of cubes to see length x breadth x height, check whether all its edges are equal, and multiply an edge in tenths by whole numbers.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: See that the cubes in a layer times the number of layers give the count, so the volume of a cuboid is length x breadth x height; tell a cube by all its edges equal; and multiply an edge in tenths by whole numbers.
writeup.look: A base layer of violet cubes with the Height handle beside it, the Edge checker on the third phase and the Tenths lens on the last.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Layer Stacker' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the number of cubes stacked. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. The solid stands in three visible faces at x 160, y 260 inside a box 600 by 400, every unit cube 40 across, its length and breadth labelled deep blue along the base. The base layer is violet, labelled Layer. The Height handle is a round grip at the solid's right edge that the child drags upward; each layer it stacks lights amber for a moment. The Units switch stands at x 820, y 250. The Edge checker's bead runs along the length, the breadth and the height in turn, and the label Cube or Cuboid appears under the solid in ink. The Tenths lens is a round glass 90 across at x 820, y 400 that rewrites an edge in tenths as a count of tenths; a card at x 820, y 500 reads Taught later when two edges have tenths. The working line runs along y 690 from x 120. The volume reached is green. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys with a point key and cu. cm and cu. m keys. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the ten tools of this chapter share them. The lengths the question gives, as a side, a length, a breadth, a height, an edge or a base area, are deep blue, labelled Given or by their own name. The perimeter, area, volume or missing side the working reaches is green, labelled Answer. The boundary that a perimeter walks round is vermilion, labelled Boundary. The unit being counted, one unit square, one unit cube, one row or one layer, is violet, labelled Unit square, Unit cube, Row or Layer. The part squares of an estimate and the space left over where no whole cube fits are rose, labelled More than half, Half or Left over. The side, square, cube, layer or step being worked on now is amber. Grey is kept for a zero holding a place open, and nothing on this stage is ever grey. A square or cube that is not being counted stays warm white inside its near-black outline, grid lines, unit words and signs are near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength. Chrome never borrows one of them, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The last solid stands stacked with its layers, labelled Cube or Cuboid, and the volume in green with its cubic unit.

writeup.delight: On the third phase, when all three edges light together, the solid gives a little spin on the spot and settles with the word Cube under it.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing yet stacked. On the first phase a base layer of cubes lies on the table top with the Height handle beside it. On the second a box lies with its edges labelled and the Units switch set. On the third a solid stands with the Edge checker's bead at one corner. On the fourth a box stands with one edge in tenths and the Tenths lens beside it. One thing moves, once: the Height handle, the Edge checker's bead or the Tenths lens gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line.
writeup.freePlay: Any base, stacked to any height, checked for equal edges or read through the Tenths lens. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on layers, length x breadth x height, cubes and edges in tenths.

voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

toolQuestions.source: props.questions ?? props.additionalProps?.questions is read; the authored rows below keep their stage (fitHost returns null).

items.planQuestion: A cuboid is 7 cubes long, 5 cubes wide and 2 cubes high. How many cubes build it?

question.en: A cuboid is 7 cubes long, 5 wide and 2 high; how many cubes build it?

items.planQuestion: A cuboid is 7 cubes long, 2 cubes wide and 2 cubes high. How many cubes build it?

question.en: Stack a cuboid 7 cubes long, 2 wide and 2 high; how many cubes is that?

items.planAnswer: One layer has 7 x 2 = 14 cubes, and 2 x 14 = 28, so 28 cubes

items.planQuestion: A cuboid is 9 cubes long, 2 cubes wide and 3 cubes high. How many cubes build it?

question.en: This one is 9 cubes long, 2 wide and 3 high; how many cubes fill it?

items.planAnswer: One layer has 9 x 2 = 18 cubes, and 3 x 18 = 54, so 54 cubes

items.planQuestion: A box is 11 cm long, 6 cm wide and 4 cm high. What is its volume?

question.en: Find the cubic centimetres in a box 11 cm long, 6 cm wide, 4 cm high.

items.planQuestion: A box is 9 cm long, 7 cm wide and 2 cm high. What is its volume?

question.en: How many cubic centimetres fill a box 9 cm by 7 cm by 2 cm?

items.planAnswer: The volume of a cuboid 9 cm long, 7 cm wide and 2 cm high is 9 x 7 x 2 = 126 cu. cm

items.planQuestion: A tank is 11 m long, 5 m wide and 2 m high. What is its volume?

question.en: A box is 11 m long, 5 m wide and 2 m high; find its volume in cubic metres.

items.planAnswer: The volume of a cuboid 11 m long, 5 m wide and 2 m high is 11 x 5 x 2 = 110 cu. m

items.planQuestion: A solid has edges of 9 cm, 9 cm and 9 cm. Is it a cube, and what is its volume?

question.en: A solid's edges are 9 cm, 9 cm and 9 cm; how many cubic centimetres is it?

items.planAnswer: Yes, it is a cube, and its volume is 729 cu. cm

items.planQuestion: A cube has edges of 10 m. What is its volume?

question.en: A cube has edges of 10 m; what is its volume in cubic metres?

items.planAnswer: The volume of a cube of edge 10 m is 10 x 10 x 10 = 1000 cu. m

items.planQuestion: A solid is 6 cm by 6 cm by 4 cm. Is it a cube?

question.en: A solid is 6 cm by 6 cm by 4 cm; is it a cube?

items.planAnswer: No. Its edges are not all equal, so it is a cuboid, not a cube

items.planQuestion: A box is 8 cm long, 3.5 cm wide and 2 cm high. What is its volume?

question.en: A box is 8 cm by 3.5 cm by 2 cm; how many cubic centimetres is its volume?

items.planQuestion: A box is 6 cm long, 2.5 cm wide and 4 cm high. What is its volume?

question.en: Find the volume of a box 6 cm by 2.5 cm by 4 cm in cubic centimetres.

items.planAnswer: 6 x 4 = 24. 2.5 cm is 25 tenths, and 25 x 24 = 600, so 600 tenths, which is 60 cu. cm

items.planQuestion: A cuboid is 4 cm long, 2.5 cm wide and 1.5 cm high. Can its volume be found by multiplying tenths by whole numbers alone?

question.en: A box 4 cm by 2.5 cm by 1.5 cm: can tenths times whole numbers give its volume?

items.planAnswer: No. Two of its edges have tenths, so it needs a decimal times a decimal, a step taught later

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once.
